newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds dip on German data, seen holding level.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds dip on German data, seen holding level.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell on higher than expected German February industrial production data on Thursday, with price levels seen holding ahead of the U.S. market opening.

"It looks like prices should hold their current levels until the end of trading here. There are jitters about the weekly U.S. jobless claims figures but Wall Street opens as we close," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.30 point down from Wednesday's close at 107.74, yielding 6.81 percent in turnover of four billion crowns.
The 2006 benchmark's June future fell 0.54 point to 106.91 with 547 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.30 point to 86.20.
The crown traded at an unchanged 3.8125 per mark at 1150 gmt.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 77.
